title: Data Types and Type Conversion
objectives: Identify int, float, str, bool types
Use type() to check variable type
Convert between types with int(), float(), str(), bool()

content.title: Python's Core Data Types
content.explanation: Every value in Python has a type. The four fundamental types are: int (integers), float (decimal numbers), str (text), and bool (True/False). The type determines what operations you can perform.

content.title: Checking Types with type()
content.explanation: type() returns the type object. Use it to inspect any value or variable.

content.title: Explicit Type Conversion
content.explanation: Convert between types using constructor functions: int(), float(), str(), bool(). Conversion may fail (ValueError) if the value cannot be converted.

content.title: Type Conversion Examples
content.code:

print(age + 5)  # 30

# Truthiness

content.explanation: Conversion functions create new values of the target type. bool() follows truthiness rules: empty/zero is False, everything else is True.

content.title: Predict Conversion Results
content.question: What does each line print?
content.explanation: int() truncates toward zero. float() adds .0. str() converts to string representation. Empty list is falsy.

content.title: Key Takeaways
points: Four core types: int, float, str, bool
Convert with int(), float(), str(), bool()
Empty/zero values are falsy; everything else is truthy
